## Fresh 20x20 diagonal test solved from demo evidence (2026-10)
Test had sparse multi-strand diagonal marks (colors 7,1,3,5) over bg0. Seven demos were requested; the decisive demo 7 (7x7) had sparse diagonal 3/9 marks and output a dense texture with period four along anti-diagonal index `r+c`: every output cell depends only on `(r+c) mod 4`. Its row0 was `[9,3,3,9,9,3,3]`; rows continue the same anti-diagonal pattern, shifting phase each row. The solved test output was a full 20x20 texture with anti-diagonal period 4 and sequence `[5,3,7,1]` indexed by `r+c mod 4`, i.e. `out[r][c] = [5,3,7,1][(r+c)%4]`. This was accepted. The sequence can be read directly from test's top-left 7 marker at (0,2), corresponding sum-index 2 ->7; color 1 on anti-diagonal at row4 col19 (sum23, mod4=3) fixes 1; color 3 on anti-diagonal sum29 (mod4=1) fixes 3; color 5 on sum32 (mod4=0) fixes 5. Practical discriminator: when sparse diagonal tracks occur and a demo shows complete output constant on `r+c` diagonals, test for a short anti-diagonal period, then infer values/order and phase from demo coordinates and test marker constraints. In this solved instance period 4 was supported by demo7's repeating 4-wide anti-diagonal pattern; other task-44bebe54 geometry variants (full-width row-stripes) follow different rules. Do not apply diagonal pattern to stripe-only inputs or infer this sequence universally.

Task ID also has diagonal-marker periodic-texture variants; classify geometry first.
